findings.body: Source consumers no longer compile, while binary-compatible implementations fail with AbstractMethodError when provider detection invokes order() during sorting.
findings.failure_mode: Crypto provider auto-detection fails before application startup instead of loading the previously valid provider.
findings.impact: Source consumers no longer compile, while binary-compatible implementations fail with AbstractMethodError when provider detection invokes order() during sorting.
findings.root_cause: A new abstract interface method was added without preserving source or binary compatibility for external CryptoProvider implementations.
findings.suggested_fix: Make order() a default method returning a documented baseline value, or provide a compatibility mechanism before invoking it on existing providers.
findings.title: Adding abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.trigger: An application or extension supplies a CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface and CryptoIntegration.init() discovers it through ServiceLoader.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds abstract method `int order()` at line 44 of CryptoProvider.java interface. External implementations compiled against prior interface lack this method, causing AbstractMethodError at runtime when CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() invokes order() during sorting. Source incompatibility is also real.

pr.body:
…tory

closes #33831

This is the Keycloak main part for solving the https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 and adding the related changes in the authz-client on the Keycloak side, which can then be later synced to the keycloak-client repository. 

In the end, I am using approach (2) from https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 with adding the method `order()` to `CryptoProvider`, which allows to have multiple instances of `CryptoProvider` on classpath (Keycloak testsuite still uses the `DefaultCryptoProvider` as before this PR).

raw_findings.root_cause: A new abstract interface method was added without preserving source or binary compatibility for external CryptoProvider implementations.

raw_findings.body: The selected provider depends on ServiceLoader resource order; a default provider can be selected instead of the FIPS/Elytron provider, or vice versa, with no startup error.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A classpath composition or resource-order change silently changes the cryptographic implementation and potentially the security mode.
raw_findings.impact: The selected provider depends on ServiceLoader resource order; a default provider can be selected instead of the FIPS/Elytron provider, or vice versa, with no startup error.
raw_findings.root_cause: Provider selection was changed from rejecting multiple providers to selecting the first sorted provider even when the highest priorities tie.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Assign unique priorities for mutually exclusive providers, or detect equal highest priorities and fail with an explicit ambiguity error.
raw_findings.title: Equal provider priorities make crypto-provider selection order-dependent
raw_findings.trigger: The runtime classpath contains more than one discovered provider with the same order, as happens with the built-in providers that all return 200.

raw_findings.body: The service-loaded provider is selected successfully but the crypto operation fails at runtime with UnsupportedOperationException.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Provider discovery succeeds while subsequent supported CryptoProvider API calls fail unexpectedly.
raw_findings.impact: The service-loaded provider is selected successfully but the crypto operation fails at runtime with UnsupportedOperationException.
raw_findings.root_cause: A CryptoProvider implementation with placeholder methods was registered as the global ServiceLoader provider.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Implement getKeyFactory using the intended JCA provider, and complete the other CryptoProvider operations required by the advertised service, or remove this partial implementation from the CryptoProvider service registration.
raw_findings.title: The registered authz crypto provider leaves key-factory operations unimplemented
raw_findings.trigger: The authz-client is used without another CryptoProvider on the classpath and a code path such as RSA key parsing calls CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getKeyFactory().

raw_findings.body: BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER is set to an unrelated provider such as SUN, causing algorithms that require Bouncy Castle or its provider-specific implementations to fail or use the wrong implementation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Provider-dependent cryptographic code is routed to an incompatible security provider.
raw_findings.impact: BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER is set to an unrelated provider such as SUN, causing algorithms that require Bouncy Castle or its provider-specific implementations to fail or use the wrong implementation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation derives a supposed Bouncy Castle provider from the default keystore implementation rather than locating or supplying Bouncy Castle.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return the actual configured Bouncy Castle provider, or do not register this implementation as a general CryptoProvider when Bouncy Castle is unavailable.
raw_findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider instead of Bouncy Castle
raw_findings.trigger: The standalone authz-client provider is selected and CryptoIntegration initialization evaluates BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER, or another crypto path requests the provider returned by getBouncyCastleProvider().

raw_findings.body: readSequence() consumes a child past the sequence boundary and accepts a non-DER encoding, allowing malformed ECDSA signature encodings to be converted as if they were valid DER.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Malformed signed input bypasses strict DER structural validation.
raw_findings.impact: readSequence() consumes a child past the sequence boundary and accepts a non-DER encoding, allowing malformed ECDSA signature encodings to be converted as if they were valid DER.
raw_findings.root_cause: The parser subtracts the consumed child length after reading it but never rejects a child that already exceeded the sequence's declared length.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Before reading each child, verify its complete encoded length does not exceed the remaining sequence length, and require the decoder to finish exactly at the declared boundary.
raw_findings.title: ASN.1 sequence parsing does not enforce the declared content boundary
raw_findings.trigger: A caller supplies a malformed DER sequence whose declared content length is shorter than the combined encoded INTEGER elements but still large enough for the first element.

raw_findings.body: The tests only verify padding and round-trip behavior for P-256 values and can pass while ES384/ES512-sized signatures or curve-specific boundary values are broken.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The test suite provides false coverage for two of the three supported ECDSA signature sizes.
raw_findings.impact: The tests only verify padding and round-trip behavior for P-256 values and can pass while ES384/ES512-sized signatures or curve-specific boundary values are broken.
raw_findings.root_cause: The parameterized algorithm tests create one default EC key before the algorithm under test is known.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Generate the key pair using secp384r1 for ES384 and secp521r1 for ES512, and retain a separate P-256 case for ES256.
raw_findings.title: ECDSA tests use a single default curve for ES384 and ES512
raw_findings.trigger: The ES384 and ES512 test cases execute with the JDK's default EC key, typically a P-256 key, rather than keys matching the algorithm's 384-bit and 521-bit curves.

finding.failure_mode: Malformed signed input bypasses strict DER structural validation.

finding.title: ASN.1 sequence parsing does not enforce the declared content boundary
finding.trigger: A caller supplies a malformed DER sequence whose declared content length is shorter than the combined encoded INTEGER elements but still large enough for the first element.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that readSequence() accepts malformed DER is speculative. The code subtracts bytes.length which includes tag+length+content of each child element. readNext() reads the complete encoded element. While boundary checking could be stricter, the claim that it 'consumes a child past the sequence boundary' is not proven by the code shown - length becomes negative if overrun, terminating the loop.
